challenges.instruction: Describe your real experience learning Somali, then make a very simple Somali version.
englishPromptLines: Write 4-5 short English sentences about your actual experience learning Somali.
Mention why you are learning, what feels easy or hard, and what you want to do next.
The AI will give you Somali words and phrase fragments, but not a full translation.
challenges.englishPlaceholder: Example: I am learning Somali because my family speaks Somali. The sounds are hard for me. I know a few greetings. I study a little every day. I want to speak with people.
challenges.somaliPlaceholder: Use the fragments to write 4-5 very short Somali sentences about your Somali learning experience.
scaffoldNotes: Focus on learning, difficulty, family, speaking, daily practice, and future wants.
Give partial Somali fragments that help the learner build their own simple sentences.
Prefer beginner forms such as waan baranayaa, way adag tahay, waan rabaa, qoyskeyga, maalin kasta.
gradingNotes: Compare the Somali draft to the learner's English notes, not to a fixed sample.
Reward simple Somali that preserves the learner's actual meaning.
A 4/5 can be short and beginner-like if it is understandable and covers most English notes.
Scores below 4 must include concrete hints for revision.

starterFragments.note: Add Somali or another thing after it.
Use if family is part of your reason.
Use if friends are part of your reason.
Use for things that are getting easier.
